item.title: A Structure-Preserving Scheme for Computing the Gradient of the Eikonal Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a first-order, structure-preserving method for directly computing the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation in smooth first-arrival regions. The method combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) in a Godunov-type upwind discretization with spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration. This construction gives a tangent residual and keeps every iterate on $\mathbb{S}^2$ without projection or normalization. The SLERP discretization exactly preserves a family of curved orientation equilibria. Removing the background discretization bias improves absolute orientation accuracy near these equilibria, allowing a prescribed error tolerance to be reached on a coarser grid. We prove the equilibrium-preservation property and, separately, a smaller angular error for SFE than normalized Euler in a one-cell relaxation under the stated step-size condition. Two- and three-dimensional experiments examine convergence, geometric preservation, and computational cost. Comparisons with gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes show more accurate directions on the same grid in the curved media considered. The method provides direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential use in adjoint-based inverse problems.
item.dc:creator: Ka Lun Leung, Shingyu Leung

item.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Diouane, Selime G\"urol, Oussama Mouhtal, Dominique Orban

item.title: Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A model for the consolidation-sedimentation process incorporating thermal effects is analysed. The model is motivated by novel applications to heat-assisted sedimentation of mineral suspensions. A system of convection-diffusion equations for the concentration and temperature are coupled to flow equations for the volume-average velocity and pressure. The model is supplemented with Dirichlet and mixed boundary conditions. A quasi-stationary approach of the system is analysed by means of a mixed variational formulation, where additional variables such as the pseudostress tensor and variables for the gradient of the temperature and concentration are introduced. The existence and uniqueness of the system is shown making use of the Babu{\v s}ka-Brezzi theory and Banach's fixed-point theorem, under hypotheses of smallness of the data and additional regularity on the solutions. A discrete formulation based on finite element spaces is proposed and analysed, and the existence of solutions is achieved thanks to Brouwer's fixed-point theorem. Additionally, C\'ea and a priori estimates are derived for the mixed formulation. Finally, numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the model and to confirm the theoretical rates of convergence.
item.dc:creator: Julio Careaga, Cristian Inzunza

item.title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an interior penalty Nitsche finite element formulation for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems, which is derived from an interior-penalty stabilized Lagrange multiplier method. A distinctive feature of the derived method is that it simultaneously combines two popular stabilization strategies: (i) a boundary penalty mechanism similar to Nitsche's methods and (ii) an interior penalty mechanism as for Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) methods. Furthermore, the normal component of the numerical flux is single-valued across the mesh skeleton and available in closed form. We establish the equivalence between the hybridized Lagrange multiplier formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche (IPN) form, and we deliver the stability and convergence analysis of the latter. For sufficiently regular solutions, we establish energy-norm error estimates for the three symmetry variants. Under a piecewise elliptic regularity assumption on the adjoint problem, the $L^2$ estimate is optimal for the symmetric variant and exhibits a half-order loss for the incomplete and nonsymmetric variants; its constant may depend on the diffusion coefficients through the adjoint regularity constant. This single-valued numerical normal flux, available in closed form, provides a starting point for locally conservative $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming flux reconstruction, left for future work. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Fontaine

item.title: Order-Specified Quaternion CP Decomposition: Models, Algorithms, and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.29370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor CP decomposition serves as a fundamental tool for representing multiway data. While quaternion tensors are well suited to modeling color visual data, extending CP decomposition to the quaternion domain is nontrivial due to the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication. This paper develops an order-specified quaternion CP decomposition (OS-QCP) for third-order tensors, allowing all three factor matrices to be quaternion-valued and explicitly incorporating their multiplication order into the model. We show that different multiplication orders can yield different OS-QCP ranks for the same quaternion tensor, characterize the permutation and quaternion scaling indeterminacies, and establish a sufficient condition for essential uniqueness for any prescribed multiplication order. An explicit example further shows that OS-QCP rank can depend on the multiplication order even when the complex representation of the quaternion tensor admits an essentially unique CP decomposition. An alternating least-squares (ALS) algorithm is derived by expressing quaternion left and right multiplication as real linear operators, reducing each factor update to real least-squares problems. To accommodate order dependence in tensor completion, we further introduce an order-ensemble quaternion CP (OE-QCP) model that incorporates different multiplication orders through nonnegative weights. The model jointly estimates three quaternion factor matrices and the order weights, with each single-order OS-QCP model included as a special case. The resulting completion problem is solved by a parallel row-wise masked ALS algorithm. Experiments on color video inpainting demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Jifei Miao, Niansheng Tang, Michael K. Ng, Juan Han, Kit Ian Kou

item.title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Significant spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal history-dependent attenuation jointly govern wave propagation in composite materials, making full-scale direct numerical simulation (DNS) computationally prohibitive. This study proposed a high-order multi-scale (HOMS) method for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems with highly oscillatory and discontinuous material coefficients. Using a multi-scale asymptotic expansion approach, the macroscopic homogenized equation, and first- and second-order correction terms are derived to construct the high-accuracy HOMS solution. Moreover, a local pointwise error analysis identifies the leading residual eliminated by this HOMS solution and validates its local physical balance preservation. Then, a global energy-norm error estimate establishes the $O(\varepsilon)$-order convergence rate for the HOMS solution. Subsequently, an efficient spatiotemporal multi-scale algorithm integrating the finite element and finite difference methods is designed, which employs a novel fully discrete $L2\text{-}1_{\sigma}$-Newmark scheme, and corresponding unconditional shifted-energy stability and explicit convergence rates are also obtained for the macroscopic homogenized displacement and velocity, respectively. Both two- and three-dimensional examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness of the proposed HOMS method. This work provides an effective multi-scale tool for nonlocal-in-time wave simulation in engineering applications.
item.dc:creator: Gehao Wang, Hao Dong, Yufeng Nie, Junzhi Cui

item.title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.29466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. Specifically, we propose using a non-uniform sampling distribution constructed from the leverage scores of the two matrices, and characterize the associated approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm; which is well-known to better characterize the downstream error when the matrix product operator is applied to an input vector. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Neophytos Charalambides, Mert Pilanci, Alfred O. Hero III

item.title: General function bases moment models for suspended sediment with vertical profile of concentration
item.description: arXiv:2610.29468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. The formulation is constructed over arbitrary vertical functional bases that are numerically orthogonalised via the Gram-Schmidt algorithm. This approach allows the approximation spaces for the vertical profile to be adapted to the specific structure of each physical variable, where also the velocity and sediment concentration can be projected onto different functional spaces. To overcome the limitations due to the inherent oscillatory nature of global Legendre polynomials, we explore a specific continuous piecewise linear $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite-element basis. Furthermore, non-uniform vertical partitions are considered, enabling an enhanced representation of the vertical profiles in specific regions. Numerical experiments involving boundary layers and suspended sediment transport demonstrate that the proposed framework is accurate to reproduce the expected vertical profiles. The improvement is particularly significant for sediment concentration profiles with sharp vertical variations, where polynomial reconstructions exhibit pronounced oscillations leading to physically meaningless profiles, whereas the $\mathbb{P}_1$ bases produce a qualitatively accurate representation of the vertical profiles observed in the sedimentation processes.
item.dc:creator: Celia Caballero-C\'ardenas, Jos\'e Garres-D\'iaz, Irene G\'omez-Bueno, Tom\'as Morales de Luna

item.title: Symmetry Inheritance and Exact Mirror Symmetry Reduction for Electric Field Vector Wave Problems with PEC Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.29481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A symmetry-inheritance and exact domain-reduction framework is developed for the second-order vector wave equation of the electric field in bounded domains with a perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary and general spatially varying anisotropic media. Orthogonal group actions on polar vectors, axial vectors, and second-order constitutive tensors are used to derive the transformed curl--curl equation and PEC trace directly from the original boundary-value problem. Under unique solvability, the common symmetry group of the problem data is inherited by the electric field. When the symmetry group of the electromagnetic medium admits a mirror symmetry, an arbitrary impressed current can be decomposed by the associated reflection projectors into mirror-even and mirror-odd components. The corresponding full-domain fields inherit the respective parities, and their exact restriction to one half-domain yields a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) condition for the even field and a PEC condition for the odd field. The original problem is therefore represented exactly by two independent reduced-domain problems. A symmetry-compatible first-family N\'ed\'elec discretization preserves this decomposition at the discrete level. Analytical and numerical results verify the symmetry-inheritance theory, the exact PEC/PMC reduced-domain formulations, and the discrete reconstruction for constant and spatially varying anisotropic conductive media under both symmetric and asymmetric excitations.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang

item.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.29516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the first tensor-product sparse-grid finite element discretizations of Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. We construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to full grids.
item.dc:creator: Yihanqi Hu, Yuwen Li

item.title: A recovery based linear finite element method for the Monge--Amp\`{e}re equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.29536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study finite element approximations of a fourth-order perturbed semilinear partial differential equation that arises naturally in the computation of viscosity solutions to the fully nonlinear Monge--Amp\`{e}re equation. We develop a novel recovery-based $C^0$ linear finite element method for discretizing this model problem. The key analytical tool is a Miranda--Talenti-type estimate for the recovery operator, which guides the formulation of the discrete scheme and guarantees its well-posedness. We rigorously establish convergence in the $H^2$ norm by employing a fixed-point argument. Furthermore, optimal $H^1$-error estimates are derived using a duality argument. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method and validate the theoretical convergence results.
item.dc:creator: Tianyang Chu, Hailong Guo, Zhimin Zhang

item.title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.29546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schr\"odinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(\delta^2)$ ($\delta >0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(\delta^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.
item.dc:creator: Jason Beh, Pierre Del Moral, Ajay Jasra

item.title: Dynamical low-rank approximations for the optimal control of matrix ODEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.29554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the open-loop optimal control of a dynamical system whose state is described by a time-dependent matrix $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$. Gradient-based optimization methods may incur substantial computational and memory costs, particularly for large-scale systems and fine temporal discretizations. To alleviate this computational burden, we develop a mathematical framework to use Dynamical Low Rank Approximations (DLRA) in optimal control problems. We study two distinct paradigms: the first one, called Optimize-then-Project (OtP), first derives the optimality system and then approximates both the state and adjoint equations using DLRA. The second one, called Project-then-Optimize (PtO), first replaces the state equation with its DLR approximation, and then derives the optimality conditions for the resulting optimization problem. The two approaches differ fundamentally concerning the role of the adjoint variable. In OtP, the adjoint variable evolves on the manifold of fixed rank matrices, whereas in PtO, the adjoint variable belongs to the tangent space to the fixed-rank manifold at the evolving state variable. This latter formulation leads to a covariant ODE describing the dynamics of the adjoint variable as the underlying tangent space evolves in time. For both approaches we establish rigorous error estimates for the approximated gradients, identifying how their accuracy depends on the low-rank approximations of initial and terminal conditions, the components of the state and adjoint vector fields normal to the relevant tangent spaces, the stability properties of the dynamics, and the manifold curvature. PtO further requires tailored time discretization strategies for the adjoint covariant ODE, which we show to be robust against small singular values of the state variable. To illustrate the framework, we apply these methods to the optimal control of a random parabolic PDE.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Carrel, Tommaso Vanzan

item.title: Parameters Robust Parallelizable Iterative Decoupled Algorithms for Thermo-Poroelasticity with Nonlinear Convective Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.29668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents several parallel iterative algorithms for the nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity. We introduce an auxiliary variable to transform the original model into a four-field formulation to overcome Poisson locking. The iterative idea is extended to linearize and decouple the four-field model. Different coupling strategies are employed among these three subproblems, combined with appropriately designed iteration settings, yielding distinct iterative parallel algorithms. Stabilization terms are incorporated into these algorithms to ensure parameter robustness in extreme situations. We derive error estimates and prove the convergence of these parallel iterative decoupled algorithms. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to compare the performance of the different parallel algorithms in extreme parameter settings, thereby validating their efficiency and robustness.
item.dc:creator: Ziliang Li, Jingzhi Li

item.title: Stability analysis of boundary element methods for the wave equation: The weakly singular operator in $1d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the construction of stable discrete pairs of trial and test spaces for the wave equation. Building on a general abstract operator-theoretic framework, we show how optimal pairings can be derived for a one-dimensional boundary element formulation of the wave equation with prescribed Dirichlet data, based on an indirect single layer potential ansatz. In this setting, the optimal test space can be computed analytically and has a physical interpretation, reflecting the non-local nature of the underlying operator.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Hoonhout, Richard L\"oscher, Carolina Urz\'ua-Torres

item.title: In vitro starch digestion kinetic, formal analysis and new kinetic model
item.description: arXiv:2610.29806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Describing mathematically the kinetics of the enzymatic hydrolysis of starch is a crucial part of nutrition and industrial applications studies. The majority of math models aim to fit the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$), so-called digestogram, whose simple shape which can be fitted equally well by various math models. A relevant model of starch digestion kinetics should be more specific of the phenomenon. This study proposes a novel analytical framework that jointly fits the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$) and the instantaneous reaction-rate coefficient ($k\_a(t)$). A large dataset comprising 672 wheat-starch time-course measurements (including normal, waxy, and high-amylose genotypes), and additional experiments on other botanical starches was analysed. Standard First-Order and Weibull models were compared with two newly derived kinetic formulations \eqref{Eq.11} and \eqref{Eq.12} based on expected starch hydrolysis' phenomenon by which $k\_a(t)$ tends with time towards an asymptotic-rate constant value, $k\_e$, following a characteristic relaxation time ($\tau$). A mathematical proof of the existence of $k\_e$, specific of the type of starch, is provided, based on an analysis of the Weibull's parameters. Model ability to fit both $X\_t$ and $k\_a(t)$ was assessed by examining coefficients of determination ($R^2$) for both data types, and its adjusted version ($R^2\_{adj}$) was used to compare performances between models. All models fit very well $X\_t$ data, while $k\_a(t)$ is much more discriminant of the model formulation. Wheat starch types are well distinguished, regarding ke, by the new models, with higher susceptibility to amylase for waxy samples ($\approx 5.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$), than normal ($\approx 2.2\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) and high-amylose ($\approx 1.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) ones. The new models outperformed the other models for monotonic evolution of $k\_a(t)$, particularly digestion of high-amylose, and allow a more accurate estimation of $k\_e$. However, the analysis also highlighted limitations for modelling non-monotonic kinetics observed for waxy wheat starch digestion, suggesting a need for more sophisticated differential-equation descriptions for $k\_a(t)$. Overall, the combined fitting strategy provides a robust method for extracting physically meaningful kinetic parameters, facilitating deeper insight into the factors controlling starch digestion and supporting the development of more accurate predictive models for glycaemic response and food processing.
item.dc:creator: Flavien Alonzo (BIA), Yuzi Wang (BIA), Luc Saulnier (BIA), Jean-Philippe Ral (CSIRO AF), Kamal Kansou (BIA)

item.title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.
item.dc:creator: Wyatt James Horne

item.title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.29871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs. The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Philippe Lessard, Akitoshi Takayasu

item.title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster
item.description: arXiv:2610.30073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration. For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.
item.dc:creator: Gilad Lerman, Teng Zhang

item.title: A linear, second-order, unconditionally energy-stable scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme for the CHQ viscoelastic phase-separation model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CHQ model describes viscoelastic phase separation in a polymer--solvent mixture: a Cahn--Hilliard equation for the polymer volume fraction $\phi$ is two-way coupled, through a phase-dependent cross-diffusion flux, to a damped relaxation equation for a scalar bulk elastic stress $q$. We propose a scalar-auxiliary-variable (SAV) time discretisation of this system, combining the SAV reformulation of the double-well potential with a second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) and a second-order extrapolation of all phase-dependent mobilities: a linear, computationally cheaper complement to the reference scheme's fully nonlinear Newton solve. The resulting method is (i) linear at every time step, with a coupling structure we prove has exactly one solution at every step, for every choice of time-step size; (ii) mass conserving, exactly, as an algebraic identity of the discrete equations themselves (the only drift ever seen numerically traces to the finite tolerance of the iterative linear solver, not a failure of the conservation property); and (iii) unconditionally stable for a modified discrete energy, via an exact one-step energy--dissipation identity. We show the energy identity extends to this filtered variant as well, with two explicit extra non-negative terms. Hence, the scheme actually producing the physics results is itself provably stable for the same energy. A Fourier--Galerkin implementation verifies that the energy identity holds at every time step to within floating-point round-off. It also confirms second-order temporal accuracy, including in the steep-interface regime, and agreement with an independently implemented nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver. Compared with that independent nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver, at equal grid resolution, the SAV method uses $2.5$--$3.0\times$ fewer linear-solver iterations and $1.7$--$2.0\times$ less wall-clock time.
item.dc:creator: Ritesh Bhola, Michael te Vrugt

item.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Mat\'ern system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Liang, Chao Chen, James Demmel, Yang Liu

item.title: DSINC beyond Heston: the 3/2 and other non-affine stochastic-volatility models
item.description: arXiv:2610.28847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper extends the damped-sinc (DSINC) method for American options beyond the affine Heston class to general one-factor stochastic-volatility models. We show that the collapse identity, which reduces the early-exercise integral to a single spectral integral, remains valid for these models. Damping between zero and one is admissible whenever the discounted spot is a nonnegative local martingale. An It\^o transformation of the volatility factorizes the conditional characteristic function and identifies a natural coordinate for approximating the exercise boundary. The 3/2 model admits closed-form joint transforms in terms of Kummer functions, while uncorrelated SABR admits a Bessel representation. When a practical closed-form transform is unavailable, the required volatility integral is computed directly by solving one backward equation per frequency, without a grid in the log-price. Through a known change of volatility coordinate, this approach also accommodates correlated SABR. Tests on the 3/2, SABR, GARCH and lognormal-volatility models show agreement with fine finite-difference benchmarks to within one basis point of the strike. Computational cost is comparable to or lower than that of our finite-difference implementation, except for the slower Hankel implementation of uncorrelated SABR.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Itkin

item.title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.29039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $\Phi_t=F_\theta^{-1}\circ\Psi_t\circ F_\theta$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $\Psi_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_\theta$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $\Psi$. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving $F_\theta$ cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to $|f|$ and sampled log-uniformly in $|x|$ around an equilibrium, with the anchors $F_\theta(0)=0$, $DF_\theta(0)=I$; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation $8.3\times10^{-3}$ and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of $F_\theta$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Qing He

item.title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.29475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-NFE generative ODE sampling is constrained not only by solver order, but also by how a fixed budget of network evaluations is distributed along the flow. We develop a density-level backward-error framework that identifies the component of a solver's modified-equation defect that changes the evolving marginal, while excluding solenoidal trajectory distortion that is invisible in Wasserstein tangent geometry. The resulting residual induces a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and, through gauge freedom, an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity representatives of the same density path. This separates our approach from schedule search driven by trajectory or endpoint surrogates and from higher-order solver design. Exact Gaussian and mixture models establish the mechanism, including cases where curvature-based allocation fails and continuum-optimal transport is not discretization-optimal. On a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM probability-flow ODE, density-aware allocation consistently improves fixed-update Euler sampling in the low-NFE regime. Matched-seed convergence to a dense Euler reference confirms that the method accelerates approximation of the same high-NFE flow rather than changing the asymptotic sampler.
item.dc:creator: Ewsey Obzherin, Valentin Khrulkov

item.title: A Super-Convergent Quasi-Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Advection-Diffusion Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.29818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of the present study is to develop discontinuous Galerkin and nonconforming finite-element methods for solving the 2D advection-diffusion equation. The discrete formulations are stabilized by means of a family of numerical fluxes and the dispersion relations are constructed via a Fourier/stability analysis. The linear discontinuous P1DG and non conforming P1NC Galerkin discretizations are studied. A long time stability result is proven for the P1NC and P1DG schemes and fluxes examined here by inspecting the discrete frequencies, solutions of the dispersion relations. A super-convergent result is also demonstrated for the P1NC discrete frequency (O(h 4 ) accuracy) compared to the P1DG one (O(h 2 ) accuracy). These results are in line with those obtained in a previous paper for the shallow-water system.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Y Le Roux (UCBL, ICJ, MMCS)

item.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.29909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schr\"odinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Toscano, Sascha Ranft, Zhiwei Gao, Li-Lian Wang, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2610.29938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\bar\omega_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\bar\omega_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.
item.dc:creator: Akram Moustafa, Jiahong Wu, Xiaoming Zheng

item.title: Random Batch Methods for Discretized PDEs on Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.11809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusion and transport processes on networks arise in applications such as pipeline systems, traffic and information flow, and energy and thermal networks. In these settings the dynamics are often modeled by partial differential equations (PDEs) on graph domains, and their simulation becomes increasingly expensive as the network size grows. The Random Batch Method (RBM) offers a way to reduce this cost, while preserving the large-scale behavior in expectation. In this paper, we study a discretize+RBM strategy for the heat equation. After a finite element discretization in space, we combine it with RBM by decomposing the resulting discrete operator into a finite sum of submatrices and, on short time intervals, replacing the full discrete operator by a randomly chosen partial sum. This defines a computationally cheaper, unbiased RBM approximation of the semi-discrete dynamics. For the one-dimensional heat equation, we prove mean-square convergence of this RBM approximation to the exact PDE solution under a suitable coupling between the short-interval length and the spatial discretization step, and we extend this analysis to a linear-quadratic optimal control problem. The same framework is then applied to the heat equation on metric graphs, and we validate it numerically, showing that the discretize+RBM scheme attains accuracy comparable to a full-graph solver while reducing computational resources. The method can be interpreted as a randomized domain-decomposition strategy on graphs. We emphasize that, beyond the heat equation, the underlying discretize+RBM construction can in principle be applied to a wider class of linear PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Martin Hernandez, Enrique Zuazua

item.title: Fast Multipole Method with Complex Coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2509.05458v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When solving problems of potential theory in unbounded layered media, recently developed integral equation methods rely on coordinate complexification to permit truncation of the computational domain while retaining high order accuracy. As a result, classical fast multipole methods (FMMs) cannot be used to accelerate the evaluation of layer potentials. In this paper, we present a variant of the FMM which applies when the source and target locations have complex coordinates in two and three dimensions. This complex coordinate FMM is based on the analytic continuation of the various special function identities used in the real-space setting. To achieve the same linear-time complexity as in the classical FMM, we construct a hierarchical tree based solely on the real parts of the complex point locations and derive convergence rates for truncated expansions when the imaginary parts of the locations depend Lipschitz-continuously on the corresponding real parts. We demonstrate the efficiency of our approach through several numerical examples and illustrate its application to solving large-scale linearized water wave problems and Helmholtz transmission problems.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Goodwill, Leslie Greengard, Jeremy Hoskins, Manas Rachh, Yuguan Wang

item.title: A survey of sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms
item.description: arXiv:2603.02459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper surveys recent developments in the sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms for functions in general finite-dimensional spaces. These results generalize the classical Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities for trigonometric and algebraic polynomials, which play a crucial role in Fourier analysis, interpolation, and approximation theory. We focus on the problem in the broad context of finite-dimensional subspaces, where norms defined by general probability measures are approximated by their discrete counterparts. The primary emphasis is on results closely related to the authors' recent research. A key objective is to highlight the main ideas and techniques that form the foundation of the proofs in this area. This survey serves as a complement to three recently published survey papers on sampling discretization \cite{DPTT, KKLT, LMT}.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Surveys in Approximation Theory, Volume 10, 2026. pp1-43
item.dc:creator: F. Dai, E. Kosov, V. Temlyakov

item.title: Dirichlet-Neumann waveform relaxation for heterogeneous heat equations: continuous and time discrete L2 analysis
item.description: arXiv:2606.29987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider two coupled linear heat equations on different spatial domains that interact through a lower dimensional interface. This models conjugate heat transfer. The problem is solved using Dirichlet--Neumann waveform relaxation. This allows us to couple separate codes for the subproblems, a so-called partitioned approach. Our overall goal is to develop more efficient partitioned methods, and to this end, we want reliable error estimates. We use an exponentially weighted Fourier technique to derive new error estimates in $L^2$ for finite time $T$ in both continuous and time-discrete settings. We identify an optimized relaxation parameter that guarantees superlinear convergence. Our new continuous estimate predicts linear convergence when $k^2/T$ is small, and superlinear when $k^2/T$ is large, with $k$ the iteration index. Our new time-discrete estimate closely mirrors its continuous counterpart for small $\Delta t$. Otherwise, we obtain linear convergence for large $k$. We also show that convergence is fast when the contrast is large, provided that the small physical parameter domain (e.g. air) is using the Dirichlet transmission condition, and the large physical parameter domain (e.g. steel) is using the Neumann transmission condition in the Dirichlet-Neumann waveform relaxation method. Numerical experiments confirm these findings, and we demonstrate the relevance on the analysis for a nonlinear conjugate heat transfer test case.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Birken, Martin J. Gander, Niklas Kotarsky, Lu-di Lu

item.title: On a boundary value problem related to radiative heat transfer
item.description: arXiv:2608.01472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the boundary value problem $y''=\kappa^2y^n, y(0)=1, y(1)=0,$ relevant to radiative heat transfer, chemical reactions, etc. We use upper/lower envelopes to study the qualitative and quantitative dependence of its solution on parameters, and transform it into an easily solvable initial value problem.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Halic

item.title: A conservative reduced collision model for the Boltzmann equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25398v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is one of the major computational bottlenecks in solving the Boltzmann equation owing to the high dimensionality and the nonlinear structure of the collision term. In this work, a conservative reduced collision (RC) model is developed within the discrete velocity framework. The bilinear collision operator is approximated through a kernel tensor preassembled with the problem-dependent reduced bases for the distribution function and the collision term. Consequently, online evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is reduced to tensor contractions. Exact discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy is enforced by constructing the collision basis in the orthogonal complement of the space spanned by the discrete collision invariants. Several numerical experiments validate the efficiency of this RC model.
item.dc:creator: Pei Zhang, Yanli Wang

item.title: Global approximations to the error function of real argument for vectorized computation
item.description: arXiv:2504.05068v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The error function of real argument can be approximated to a given uniform relative accuracy by a single closed-form expression for the whole variable range either in terms of addition, multiplication, division, and square root operations only, or also using the exponential function. Approximations to the complementary error function have also been found, including those where either only additions, multiplications, and one division, or also the exponential, are used to reach either a uniform absolute, or a uniform relative, accuracy. The coefficients have been tabulated for up to 128-bit precision. Tests of a computer code implementation using the standard single- and double-precision floating-point arithmetic show good performance and vectorizability.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri N. Laikov

item.title: Families of relative periodic orbits in the planar three-body problem via consecutive alignments
item.description: arXiv:2609.01585v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relative periodic orbits (RPOs) are solutions of the three-body problem that are periodic in a uniformly rotating reference frame and, in general, quasi-periodic in inertial coordinates. We present a numerical procedure for computing and continuing one-parameter families of RPOs of the planar Newtonian three-body problem. The method exploits consecutive syzygies, understood here as configurations in which the three bodies are aligned and their velocities satisfy the corresponding symmetry conditions. Matching the positions and momenta at two consecutive alignments reduces the computation of RPOs to a low-dimensional nonlinear problem. Its solutions are then numerically continued, and linear stability is determined from the nontrivial eigenvalues of the rotated monodromy matrix after removing the neutral directions associated with conserved quantities and continuous symmetries. The procedure is applied to several mass distributions and initial configurations, producing families of Poincar\'e, Hill, and binary-type solutions. These families exhibit transitions from nearly circular to highly eccentric motion, changes of stability near resonances and turning points, and absolute periodic solutions when the rotation angle is a rational multiple of 2{\pi}. In the Hill families, the continuation connects satellite configurations with circumstellar motion as the smallest body loses its gravitational binding to the intermediate body. Circumbinary and circumstellar configurations are also obtained in the binary regime. The results illustrate the dynamical diversity of RPOs and provide coherent three-body motions that can be used as prescribed trajectories in restricted four-body models.
item.dc:creator: Joan Gimeno, Marc Jorba-Cusc\'o, Bego\~na Nicol\'as

item.title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. Numerical optimization involving stiff evolutionary and static PDEs often requires solving a large system of equations, which can be treated as a constraint. In this work, we present a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver that incorporates this constraint. We evaluate its performance across four key tasks: a) linear and nonlinear forward modeling of evolutionary and static problems, b) solving inverse problems to estimate equation coefficients, c) solving inverse problems to estimate the right-hand side, and d) learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. These capabilities make it a powerful tool for different physics and engineering applications, in particular for geophysics, where inverse problems are commonly solved in order to reduce the model uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Yavich, Alexander Ryabov, Viacheslav Naumov, Sayan Ranu, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Evgeny Burnaev, Vladimir Vanovskiy
